stories.title: Senior police officers in South Korea’s Jeju removed from duty over missing-person scandal
stories.summary: Four senior officers at Jeju Seobu. Police Station were suspended after a police officer falsely closed missing-person cases, including that of Jang Mi-ran, who was later found dead. The officer, Bu, is charged with dereliction of duty and falsifying records; police are reviewing 298 cases he handled to check for similar misconduct. The scandal sparked a nationwide review of closed missing-person cases and led to promises of stronger verification before cases can be closed in future. The Jeju missing-person scandal deepened on Aug 25 as senior officers were removed from duty and new details emerged about how a police officer allegedly falsely closed cases involving two people who were later found dead. Police Station have been suspended from their duties in connection with the cases, the National. Police Agency (NPA) said. The officer at the centre of the investigation, surnamed Bu, is accused of closing missing-person cases after falsely claiming to have confirmed the safety of those reported missing. The four officers removed from duty are the current chief of Jeju Seobu. Police Station, the chief who headed the station when 37-year-old Jang Mi-ran was reported missing, the head of the detective division, and the leader of the team handling missing-person cases. The NPA said it is conducting an internal inspection to determine whether the officers properly supervised the handling of the cases, and whether they should be held responsible for failures in command and oversight. The case has escalated into a broader examination of Korea’s missing-person system, raising questions over how a lower-ranking officer could close cases without properly verifying people’s safety and whether supervisors failed to catch repeated problems.

stories.title: Iran and Oman discuss temporary corridor in Strait or Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran and Oman held talks in Tehran to discuss the management of traffic passing through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as a joint mine-clearing project. Further negotiations are expected to discuss a permanent solution.

stories.title: Houthi leader underlines support for Palestinians, slams Saudi 'tyranny'
stories.summary: Houthi leader underlines support for Palestinians, slams Saudi 'tyranny' Houthi leader Abdel-Malik al-Houthi has restated support for Palestinian fighters, according to the Houthi-run SABA news agency, saying they would "spare no effort" in backing the Palestinian people until the fall of Israel. In the statement, he also accused the Saudi Arabia of committing "tyranny and injustice" against the Yemeni people, adding that the situation demanded "new moves using all legitimate means" to counter Riyadh’s policies. Houthi also condemned what he called as an "unjust siege" and "aggressive occupation" carried out by Riyadh with US backing.
